title: OpenCode v2 / Super Pi Codemode bounded library comparison
evidenceClass: M: measured local fixtures, not product-level performance

temporaryResources.cleanup: Deletion request rejected by automatic approval: blocked by policy. Directory retained; no cleanup workaround attempted.

method.scope: Library execution only; static imports and host creation excluded; Pi fresh Worker creation and termination included; OpenCode make_each includes CodeMode.make only, not core adapter tree/progress/web/policy.
caveats: Node is a common comparison runtime; OpenCode application uses Bun.
Output limits differ in bytes vs UTF-16 chars; fixtures are ASCII.
No real model, network, disk, policy, UI or complete product/token-cost comparison.
Reused OpenCode runtime is library best case, not core adapter reuse.
Timing does not compare total allocations, peak heap or event-loop responsiveness.
15 samples describe this local run, not a statistically stable production p95.
Pi imports source .ts files and launches its source-mode Worker; packaged/compiled application latency was not measured.
Both runtimes use the same three plain-data fixture tools; OpenCode render-only JSON Schema does not add input/output schema validation in this harness.
The parallel fixture measures library-level fan-out; it does not include Pi's product-level read concurrency=4 and serialized mutation policy.

reproduction.notes: Download only the fixed commit packages/codemode/src tree into an isolated temporary directory, create a private ESM package.json with the pinned dependencies, and install with --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund. Create wrapper.ts from main.reproduction.wrapper, bundle with the recorded esbuild command (the repo's existing esbuild was used), then save the exact harness below as compare.mjs. Replace its two D:/RMProjects/Pi file URLs with the local checkout path. Source downloads and temporary dependencies are not vendored.
